environment.database: isolated Postgres 18 container, port 55432, throwaway credentials, seeded
environment.app: production build (npm run start) on port 3100
environment.note: The developer's own instance occupies port 3000 against a different database. A first attempt probed that instance by mistake and produced 17 false 5xx results; those are discarded. Only the port-3100 run is reported here.

findings.finding: Runtime probing confirms every protected route refuses unauthenticated access correctly: 32 page routes redirect 307 to /admin/login with a callbackUrl, 6 API routes return 401, and no route returns 5xx
evidence: qa/reports/route-smoke.json — 74 routes probed, mode EXECUTED, status distribution 200x20 307x32 401x6 404x10 405x5 400x1
qa/reports/evidence/db-run-001/check-db.log — all six migration suites passed first
src/proxy.ts:18 — the optimistic cookie check that produces the 307
reproduction: Start Postgres 18 in a container on 55432 and apply migrations with an explicit DATABASE_URL
Seed, build, and start the app on port 3100 against that database
findings.expected: Protected pages redirect to login; protected APIs return 401; nothing leaks a 500
findings.user_impact: None — this is the positive result. It empirically confirms the static verified-negative from phase 5, which had only established that guards were present in code, not that their failure mode was correct
findings.recommendation: No action. Record as the runtime baseline for regression comparison

findings.feature: check:db is not in CI's required path for local work
findings.finding: The six database verification suites pass, and they are the project's only functional coverage — but they had never been run during this QA effort, and eight fixes were applied and shipped as verified on typecheck, lint and build alone
evidence: qa/reports/evidence/db-run-001/seed.log — seeding succeeded against the isolated database
.github/workflows/check.yml — CI does run check:db, so the gate exists upstream
package.json — check:db requires a database and is therefore skipped by default locally
reproduction: Observe that the eight fixes in this run were marked verified before any suite requiring a database had been executed
Run check:db against an isolated database — it passes, and would have caught a schema-level regression
findings.expected: A fix touching deletion guards, authorization and rate limiting is verified by something that executes it
findings.actual: Verified by typecheck, lint, 19 unit tests over unrelated files, and a production build. The suites that exercise the schema existed and were not run until now
findings.root_cause: Running them needs a database, and nothing in the local workflow provisions one, so the step is skipped rather than failed
findings.user_impact: Regressions in the operational schema reach CI rather than being caught locally
findings.recommendation: Use scripts/env-bootstrap.mjs to provision a disposable database and make check:db part of the local pre-commit path. The suites already exist and already pass — only the provisioning was missing

findings.finding: Production-build response times across 74 routes: 41ms median, 160ms p90, 516ms max, with no route exceeding 1500ms
evidence: qa/reports/route-smoke.json — per-route durationMs for all 74 routes
reproduction: Production build on port 3100 against the seeded isolated database
route-smoke with --slow=1500, concurrency 4, single unwarmed request per route
findings.expected: No stated performance target exists in the project, so this is a baseline rather than a pass or fail
findings.user_impact: None observed. Conditions: production build, seeded demo dataset (8 projects, 12 activities, 6 documents), single unwarmed request, concurrency 4, local loopback. Not representative of production data volume
findings.recommendation: Adopt this as the baseline and set an explicit p95 target so future measurements have something to fail against
